```text
# Draft issue: partial-day out-of-office badge and redirect

Drafted 2026-10-18 for `zach-short`. Not posted. Private, untracked.

## How to post (for Zach, after review)

- Title: `Show the away badge and redirect for partial-day out-of-office entries`
- Labels to propose: `enhancement`, `effort:medium`. Both exist (`gh label list -R CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy`, read 2026-10-18). The template adds `✨ feature` and `🚨 needs approval` on its own, if those labels exist on this fork. Neither is in the label list, so check what GitHub actually applies.
- Template: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md`. The body below keeps its headings and adds the sections issue #6 used (User Story, User Scenario, Acceptance Criteria, Out of Scope, Open Questions, Technical Notes), so it reads like #6.
- Milestone: Sprint 2, once PASSOFF item 23 creates it.
- The template ends with a "House rules" footer. This draft leaves it out because its wording breaks the writing rules for this file. When you post through the GitHub form, the form fills that footer in. Keep it there. For the same reason one heading reads "you would like" here. Keep the form's own heading text.
- Duplicate check: `gh issue list -R CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy --state all --search "out of office partial"` returns only #6 (closed by PR #85).
- Code citations are from `origin/main` at `cc65a9670f` (2026-10-12). The local branch `short` does not contain PR #85, so its line numbers differ. Check the citations again on the branch you cut for this issue.

Everything below the line is the issue body.

---

### Is your proposal related to a problem?

PR #85 (closes #6) lets a host set a leave time and a return time on an out-of-office entry. The booking page now removes the slots inside that window, but it does that the way it removes a calendar event: the slots are gone, and nothing says why. A whole-day entry shows the "away" panel with the reason, the emoji, the public note and, when a redirect user is set, a "Book with <name>" button. A partial-day entry shows none of these. PR #85 names this as a known limit ("Partial-day entries do not show the "away" badge or a redirect on the booking page") and describes "alternative 1" as the path to fix it.

### Describe the solution you would like

Build alternative 1 from PR #85: teach the per-day out-of-office map about time ranges. Slots inside a partial-day window stay in the slot list, marked `away` with the entry's reason, emoji, note and redirect user, the same data a whole-day entry carries. The booker then renders one "away" panel at the place in the day where the window falls, between the slots before it and the slots after it. Away slots stay unbookable, as they are for whole days today.

### User Story

As an attendee who opens a host's booking page, I want to see that the host is away for part of the day, and book with their redirect user if one is set, so that I know why some times are missing and where to book instead.

### User Scenario

A host works 09:00 to 17:00 and has a partial-day entry from 14:00 to 16:00 with the reason "Doctor" and a public note. An attendee opens the booking page for that day. Slots from 09:00 run up to the slot that ends at 14:00. Below them is the away panel with the emoji, the reason and the note. Below the panel, slots resume at 16:00. If the entry has a redirect user, the panel also shows "Book with <name>", and the button opens that user's booking page on the same date.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. For a partial-day entry, every slot that overlaps the window is returned with `away: true` and the entry's `fromUser`, `toUser`, `reason`, `emoji`, and the note when `showNotePublicly` is on. Slots that do not overlap the window have no `away` flag.
2. A slot marked away for a partial-day entry cannot be booked. Booking it returns the same error as booking inside a whole-day entry.
3. On the booking page, a day with a partial-day window shows the bookable slots before the window, one away panel, and the bookable slots after the window, in that order. This holds when the window is at the start of the day, in the middle, or at the end.
4. When the entry has a redirect user, the away panel shows "Book with <name>", and clicking it opens that user's booking page on the same date, as it does for a whole-day entry.
5. A partial-day entry that covers all of the host's working hours on a day renders that day exactly as a whole-day entry does, in the time list and in the date picker.
6. Whole-day entries, holidays and calendar busy times render and block exactly as before. Existing tests for them pass unchanged.
7. API v2 slot responses do not change. Away slots stay filtered out of them (`slots-output.service.ts:49` and `:119` already do this).
8. Unit tests cover criteria 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6, including a window on a DST change day in America/New_York.

### Out of Scope

- Setting a redirect user from the out-of-office form. The redirect switch is disabled in this fork (`hasTeamPlan = false`, `CreateOrEditOutOfOfficeModal.tsx:190`, used at `:483`). This issue only renders a redirect that is already stored.
- Partial-day entries through API v2, which still stores whole days (PR #85, Known limits).
- Team and round-robin events. Their availability uses `oooExcludedDateRanges` (`getAggregatedAvailability.ts:43` and `:65`), so whole-day entries show no away panel there either.
- Changes to the out-of-office form or list from PR #85.

### Open Questions

- Which slots count as "inside" the window? A 30-minute event at 13:45 overlaps a 14:00 leave time. Criterion 1 says any overlap marks the slot away. The other option is to drop overlapping slots and mark only the slots fully inside the window. A window shorter than one slot interval (for example 14:10 to 14:20) may otherwise produce no away slot and so no panel.
- What does the panel say for a 2-hour entry? Today it says the host is away with no times. Should a partial-day panel show the leave and return times ("Away 2:00 PM to 4:00 PM")? That needs a new string in `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json` and the times in the attendee's timezone, not the host's.
- Two partial-day entries on one day (for example 10:00 to 11:00 and 14:00 to 15:00): two panels, or one? The per-day map holds one entry per date today, so this decides the shape of the data.
- Timezone edges. The map is keyed by the host's date (`slots.ts:189-192` formats the slot in `datesOutOfOfficeTimeZone`). An attendee several hours away can see a host's evening window on their next day. Is it enough that the panel sits between the right slots in the attendee's view, or must the panel also say the host's local times?
- The redirect cannot be set from the UI or from API v2 in this fork today. Is criterion 4 worth keeping if it can be shown only with a unit test and a hand-edited `OutOfOfficeEntry.toUserId` row?

### Technical Notes (from reading the code, to be confirmed while implementing)

Line numbers are from `origin/main` at `cc65a9670f`.

- **Where partial entries leave the map today.** `UserAvailabilityService.calculateOutOfOfficeRanges` returns early for any entry that fails `isWholeDayOutOfOffice` (`packages/features/availability/lib/getUserAvailability.ts:748`). The predicate is at `packages/features/schedules/lib/date-ranges.ts:228`. The partial entries go to `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeRanges` instead (`date-ranges.ts:248`, called at `getUserAvailability.ts:482`).
- **Why the slots vanish.** The partial ranges are appended to the busy times (`getUserAvailability.ts:651-657`) and subtracted from both `dateRanges` and `oooExcludedDateRanges` (`:659-660`). A whole-day entry is different: it stays in `dateRanges`, so its slots are generated and then marked away, and it is removed only from `oooExcludedDateRanges` through `groupedOOO` (`date-ranges.ts:297-300` and `:354-361`). To get away slots, a partial window must follow the same split: subtract it from `oooExcludedDateRanges` only, and keep it in `dateRanges`.
- **Booking stays blocked.** `ensureAvailableUsers` checks a booking against `oooExcludedDateRanges` (`packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/ensureAvailableUsers.ts:220`), so once the window is removed there, a booking inside it is still rejected. Criterion 2 needs a test for this.
- **Slot marking is date-level.** `buildSlotsWithDateRanges` looks up `datesOutOfOffice[YYYY-MM-DD]` and marks every slot on that date (`packages/features/schedules/lib/slots.ts:187-221`). It needs a time check for partial entries. `IOutOfOfficeData` (`getUserAvailability.ts:209`) maps a date to one entry, so the type must carry the window (for example optional `start` and `end`, or a list per date). See the open question on two entries in one day.
- **The booker assumes away means a whole day.** `AvailableTimes` shows the panel when every slot is away, or when only the first or only the last slot is away, and it hides every away slot (`apps/web/modules/bookings/components/AvailableTimes.tsx:266-293`). A mid-day window has neither its first nor its last slot away, so no panel renders. It must render the panel at the first away slot of each run. `AvailableTimeSlots` decides that a day is away from its first slot only (`apps/web/modules/bookings/components/AvailableTimeSlots.tsx:206`, comment "since OOO is date-level"), which hides the time-format toggle when a window starts the day.
- **The redirect.** The "Book with" button is in `OutOfOfficeInSlots.tsx`, which calls `router.push` to `/${toUser.username}` with the date. It already works from the slot data, so criterion 4 needs only the data in criterion 1.
- **Other readers of `away`.** `DatePicker.tsx:256-269` marks a day as away only when every slot is away, which gives criterion 5 for free. `useNonEmptyScheduleDays.ts:13` and the weekly view `Empty.tsx:66` also read the flag. Check that they do not change for a partial window.
- **Test that must change.** PR #85 added `getUserAvailability.outOfOffice.timezone.test.ts`, which asserts that a partial-day entry "stays off the away map". This issue reverses that on purpose. Update the case, do not delete it.
- **DST.** Keep the `wallClockToTimeZone` parse from PR #85 (`date-ranges.ts:241-246`) for the window edges. `.tz(zone, true)` returns the wrong offset near a DST change.

### Additional context

Estimate: medium (`effort:medium`). The likely files are `getUserAvailability.ts`, `date-ranges.ts`, `slots.ts`, `AvailableTimes.tsx`, `AvailableTimeSlots.tsx`, plus `slots.test.ts`, `date-ranges.test.ts`, `getUserAvailability.outOfOffice.timezone.test.ts`, and a new test for `AvailableTimes`. That is about 5 code files and 4 test files, under the 10-file limit in `AGENTS.md`. The slot engine part reuses a pattern that whole-day entries already use, which keeps it medium. The booker change is the part that could grow, because no unit test covers `AvailableTimes` today (`apps/web/modules/bookings/components/` has tests only for `Booker`, `BookingDetailsSheet` and `DatePicker`). If the diff passes 500 lines, split it: engine and slots first, booker second.

- Issue #6: https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/issues/6
```

```text
export interface IFromUser {
  id: number;
  displayName: string | null;
}

export interface IToUser {
  id: number;
  username: string | null;
  displayName: string | null;
}

export interface IOutOfOfficeData {
  [key: string]: {
    fromUser: IFromUser | null;
    toUser?: IToUser | null;
    reason?: string | null;
    emoji?: string | null;
    notes?: string | null;
    showNotePublicly?: boolean;
  };
}

export interface IUserAvailabilityService {
  eventTypeRepo: EventTypeRepository;
  oooRepo: PrismaOOORepository;
  bookingRepo: BookingRepository;
  redisClient: IRedisService;
  holidayRepo: PrismaHolidayRepository;
}

export class UserAvailabilityService {
  constructor(public readonly dependencies: IUserAvailabilityService) {}

  // Fetch timezones from outlook or google using delegated credentials (formely known as domain wide delegatiion)
  async getTimezoneFromDelegatedCalendars(user: NonNullable<GetAvailabilityUser>): Promise<string | null> {
    if (!user.credentials || user.credentials.length === 0) {
      return null;
    }

    const workingHours = getWorkingHours({ timeZone: finalTimezone }, availability);

    const dateOverrides: TimeRange[] = [];
    // NOTE: getSchedule is currently calling this function for every user in a team event
    // but not using these values at all, wasting CPU. Adding this check here temporarily to avoid a larger refactor
    // since other callers do using this data.
    if (returnDateOverrides) {
      const calculateDateOverridesSpan = Sentry.startInactiveSpan({ name: "calculateDateOverrides" });
      const availabilityWithDates = availability.filter((availability) => !!availability.date);

      for (let i = 0; i < availabilityWithDates.length; i++) {
        const override = availabilityWithDates[i];
        const startTime = dayjs.utc(override.startTime);
        const endTime = dayjs.utc(override.endTime);
        const overrideStartDate = dayjs.utc(override.date).hour(startTime.hour()).minute(startTime.minute());
        const overrideEndDate = dayjs.utc(override.date).hour(endTime.hour()).minute(endTime.minute());
        if (
          overrideStartDate.isBetween(dateFrom, dateTo, null, "[]") ||
          overrideEndDate.isBetween(dateFrom, dateTo, null, "[]")
        ) {
          dateOverrides.push({
            start: overrideStartDate.toDate(),
            end: overrideEndDate.toDate(),
          });
        }
      }

      calculateDateOverridesSpan.end();
    }

    const outOfOfficeDays =
      initialData?.outOfOfficeDays ??
      (await this.dependencies.oooRepo.findUserOOODays({
        userId: user.id,
        dateFrom: dateFrom.toISOString(),
        dateTo: dateTo.toISOString(),
      }));

    // Whole-day entries fill the per-day "away" map the booker renders. Entries with a time of day block
    // only their window: they are subtracted together with the busy times below and never reach the map.
    const datesOutOfOffice: IOutOfOfficeData = this.calculateOutOfOfficeRanges(outOfOfficeDays, availability);
    const partialDayOutOfOfficeRanges = getPartialDayOutOfOfficeRanges(outOfOfficeDays, finalTimezone);

    const holidayBlockedDates = await this.calculateHolidayBlockedDates(
      user.id,
      dateFrom.toDate(),
      dateTo.toDate(),
      availability
    );

    for (const [date, holidayData] of Object.entries(holidayBlockedDates)) {
      if (!datesOutOfOffice[date]) {
        datesOutOfOffice[date] = holidayData;
      }
    }

    const travelSchedules: {
      startDate: Dayjs;
      endDate?: Dayjs;
      timeZone: string;
    }[] = [];

    if (isDefaultSchedule) {
      travelSchedules.push(
        ...user.travelSchedules.map((schedule) => {
          let endDate: Dayjs | undefined;
          if (schedule.endDate) {
            endDate = dayjs(schedule.endDate);
          }
          return {
            startDate: dayjs(schedule.startDate),
            endDate,
            timeZone: schedule.timeZone,
          };
        })
      );
    }

    const { dateRanges, oooExcludedDateRanges } = buildDateRanges({
      dateFrom,
      dateTo,
      availability,
      timeZone: finalTimezone,
      travelSchedules,
      outOfOffice: datesOutOfOffice,
    });

    if (dateRanges.length === 0)
      return {
        busy: [],
        timeZone: finalTimezone,
        dateRanges: [],
        oooExcludedDateRanges: [],
        workingHours: [],
        dateOverrides: [],
        currentSeats: [],
        datesOutOfOffice: undefined,
      };

    const { bookingLimits, durationLimits } = await this.parseLimits(eventType);

    // TODO: only query what we need after applying limits (shrink date range)
    const getBusyTimesStart = dateFrom.toISOString();
    const getBusyTimesEnd = dateTo.toISOString();

    const selectedCalendars = eventType?.useEventLevelSelectedCalendars
      ? user.allSelectedCalendars.filter((calendar) => calendar.eventTypeId === eventType.id)
      : user.userLevelSelectedCalendars;

    let busyTimesFromLimits: EventBusyDetails[] = [];
    if (initialData?.busyTimesFromLimits && initialData?.eventTypeForLimits) {
      busyTimesFromLimits = initialData.busyTimesFromLimits.get(user.id) || [];
    } else if (eventType && (bookingLimits || durationLimits)) {
      busyTimesFromLimits = await getBusyTimesFromLimits(
        bookingLimits,
        durationLimits,
        dateFrom.tz(finalTimezone),
        dateTo.tz(finalTimezone),
        duration,
        eventType,
        initialData?.busyTimesFromLimitsBookings ?? [],
        finalTimezone,
        initialData?.rescheduleUid ?? undefined
      );
    }

    const teamForBookingLimits =
      initialData?.teamForBookingLimits ??
      eventType?.team ??
      (eventType?.parent?.team?.includeManagedEventsInLimits ? eventType?.parent?.team : null);

    const teamBookingLimits = parseBookingLimit(teamForBookingLimits?.bookingLimits);

    let busyTimesFromTeamLimits: EventBusyDetails[] = [];

    if (initialData?.teamBookingLimits && teamForBookingLimits) {
      busyTimesFromTeamLimits = initialData.teamBookingLimits.get(user.id) || [];
    } else if (teamForBookingLimits && teamBookingLimits) {
      // Fall back to individual query if not available in initialData
      busyTimesFromTeamLimits = await getBusyTimesFromTeamLimits(
        user,
        teamBookingLimits,
        dateFrom.tz(finalTimezone),
        dateTo.tz(finalTimezone),
        teamForBookingLimits.id,
        teamForBookingLimits.includeManagedEventsInLimits,
        finalTimezone,
        initialData?.rescheduleUid ?? undefined
      );
    }

    let busyTimes = [];
    try {
      const busyTimesService = getBusyTimesService();
      busyTimes = await busyTimesService.getBusyTimes({
        credentials: user.credentials,
        startTime: getBusyTimesStart,
        endTime: getBusyTimesEnd,
        eventTypeId,
        userId: user.id,
        userEmail: user.email,
        username: `${user.username}`,
        beforeEventBuffer,
        afterEventBuffer,
        selectedCalendars,
        seatedEvent: !!eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot,
        rescheduleUid: initialData?.rescheduleUid || null,
        duration,
        currentBookings: initialData?.currentBookings,
        bypassBusyCalendarTimes,
        silentlyHandleCalendarFailures,
        mode,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      log.error(`Error fetching busy times for user ${username}:`, error);
      return {
        busy: [],
        timeZone: finalTimezone,
        dateRanges: [],
        oooExcludedDateRanges: [],
        workingHours: [],
        dateOverrides: [],
        currentSeats: [],
        datesOutOfOffice: undefined,
      };
    }

    const detailedBusyTimesWithSource: EventBusyDetails[] = [
      ...busyTimes.map((a) => ({
        ...a,
        start: dayjs(a.start).toISOString(),
        end: dayjs(a.end).toISOString(),
        title: a.title,
        source: a.source,
      })),
      ...busyTimesFromLimits,
      ...busyTimesFromTeamLimits,
    ];

    const detailedBusyTimes: UserAvailabilityBusyDetails[] = withSource
      ? detailedBusyTimesWithSource
      : detailedBusyTimesWithSource.map(({ source, ...rest }) => rest);

    log.debug(
      `EventType: ${eventTypeId} | User: ${username} (ID: ${userId}) - usingSchedule: ${safeStringify({
        chosenSchedule: schedule,
        eventTypeSchedule: eventType?.schedule,
      })}`
    );

    const formattedBusyTimes = [
      ...detailedBusyTimes.map((busy) => ({
        start: dayjs(busy.start),
        end: dayjs(busy.end),
      })),
      ...partialDayOutOfOfficeRanges,
    ];

    const dateRangesInWhichUserIsAvailable = subtract(dateRanges, formattedBusyTimes);
    const dateRangesInWhichUserIsAvailableWithoutOOO = subtract(oooExcludedDateRanges, formattedBusyTimes);

    const result = {
      busy: detailedBusyTimes,
      timeZone: finalTimezone,
      dateRanges: dateRangesInWhichUserIsAvailable,
      oooExcludedDateRanges: dateRangesInWhichUserIsAvailableWithoutOOO,
      workingHours,
      dateOverrides,
      currentSeats,
      datesOutOfOffice,
    };

    log.debug(
      `EventType: ${eventTypeId} | User: ${username} (ID: ${userId}) - Result: ${safeStringify(result)}`
    );

    return result;
  }

  /**
   * This fn mainly uses _getUserAvailability but sends busy times from limits too to _getUserAvailability as expected by _getUserAvailability.
   */
  async getUserAvailabilityIncludingBusyTimesFromLimits(
    params: GetUserAvailabilityParams,
    initialData: Ensure<GetUserAvailabilityInitialData, "user">
  ): Promise<GetUserAvailabilityResult> {
    const { user } = initialData || {};
    const { dateFrom, dateTo, eventTypeId } = params;
    let eventType: EventType | null = initialData?.eventType || null;
    if (!eventType && eventTypeId) eventType = await this.getEventType(eventTypeId);

    const { bookingLimits, durationLimits } = await this.parseLimits(eventType);

    let busyTimesFromLimitsBookings: EventBusyDetails[] | undefined =
      initialData?.busyTimesFromLimitsBookings;
    if (!busyTimesFromLimitsBookings && eventType && (bookingLimits || durationLimits)) {
      const busyTimesService = getBusyTimesService();
      const { limitDateFrom, limitDateTo } = busyTimesService.getStartEndDateforLimitCheck(
        dateFrom.toISOString(),
        dateTo.toISOString(),
        bookingLimits,
        durationLimits
      );

      // For team events with booking/duration limits, fetch bookings for all team members
```

```text
import type { DateRange } from "@calcom/features/schedules/lib/date-ranges";
import { intersect } from "@calcom/features/schedules/lib/date-ranges";
import { DEFAULT_GROUP_ID } from "@calcom/lib/constants";
import { SchedulingType } from "@calcom/prisma/enums";

import { filterRedundantDateRanges } from "./date-range-utils/filterRedundantDateRanges";
import { mergeOverlappingDateRanges } from "./date-range-utils/mergeOverlappingDateRanges";

function uniqueAndSortedDateRanges(ranges: DateRange[]): DateRange[] {
  const seen = new Set<string>();

  return ranges
    .sort((a, b) => {
      const startDiff = a.start.valueOf() - b.start.valueOf();
      return startDiff !== 0 ? startDiff : a.end.valueOf() - b.end.valueOf();
    })
    .filter((range) => {
      const key = `${range.start.valueOf()}-${range.end.valueOf()}`;
      if (seen.has(key)) return false;
      seen.add(key);
      return true;
    });
}

export const getAggregatedAvailability = (
  userAvailability: {
    dateRanges: DateRange[];
    oooExcludedDateRanges: DateRange[];
    user?: { isFixed?: boolean; groupId?: string | null };
  }[],
  schedulingType: SchedulingType | null
): DateRange[] => {
  const isTeamEvent =
    schedulingType === SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE ||
    schedulingType === SchedulingType.ROUND_ROBIN ||
    userAvailability.length > 1;

  const fixedHosts = userAvailability.filter(
    ({ user }) => !schedulingType || schedulingType === SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE || user?.isFixed
  );

  const fixedDateRanges = mergeOverlappingDateRanges(
    intersect(fixedHosts.map((s) => (!isTeamEvent ? s.dateRanges : s.oooExcludedDateRanges)))
  );
  const dateRangesToIntersect = fixedDateRanges.length ? [fixedDateRanges] : [];
  const roundRobinHosts = userAvailability.filter(({ user }) => user?.isFixed !== true);
  if (roundRobinHosts.length) {
    // Group round robin hosts by their groupId
    const hostsByGroup = roundRobinHosts.reduce(
      (groups, host) => {
        const groupId = host.user?.groupId || DEFAULT_GROUP_ID;
        if (!groups[groupId]) {
          groups[groupId] = [];
        }
        groups[groupId].push(host);
        return groups;
      },
      {} as Record<string, typeof roundRobinHosts>
    );

    // at least one host from each group needs to be available
    Object.values(hostsByGroup).forEach((groupHosts) => {
      if (groupHosts.length > 0) {
        const groupDateRanges = groupHosts.flatMap((s) =>
          !isTeamEvent ? s.dateRanges : s.oooExcludedDateRanges
        );
        dateRangesToIntersect.push(groupDateRanges ?? []);
      }
    });
  }

  const availability = intersect(dateRangesToIntersect);

  const uniqueRanges = uniqueAndSortedDateRanges(availability);

  return filterRedundantDateRanges(uniqueRanges);
};
```

```text
   271	  // Display ooo in slots once but after or before slots

   273	  const oooAfterSlots = slots[slots.length - 1] && slots[slots.length - 1].away;

   283	            <p className={classNames("text-muted", showTimeFormatToggle ? "-mt-1 text-lg" : "text-sm")}>
   284	              {t("all_booked_today")}
   285	            </p>
   286	          </div>
   287	        )}
   288	        {oooBeforeSlots && !oooAfterSlots && <OOOSlot {...slots[0]} />}
   289	        {slots.map((slot) => {
   290	          if (slot.away) return null;
   291	          return <SlotItem key={slot.time} slot={slot} {...props} />;
   292	        })}
   293	        {oooAfterSlots && !oooBeforeSlots && <OOOSlot {...slots[slots.length - 1]} className="pb-0" />}
   294	      </div>
   295	    </div>
   296	  );
   297	};
```

```text
interface IOutOfOfficeInSlotsProps {

  className?: string;
}

export const OutOfOfficeInSlots = (props: IOutOfOfficeInSlotsProps) => {
  const { t } = useLocale();
  const {
    fromUser,
    toUser,
    emoji = "🏝️",
    reason,
    borderDashed = true,
    date,
    className,
    notes,
    showNotePublicly,
  } = props;
  const searchParams = useCompatSearchParams();

  const router = useRouter();

  // Check if this is a holiday (no fromUser but has reason)
  const isHoliday = !fromUser && reason;

  // For regular OOO, require fromUser (toUser is optional for redirect)

  if (!isHoliday && !fromUser) return null;
  return (
    <div className={classNames("relative h-full pb-5", className)}>
      <div
        className={classNames(
          "flex h-full flex-col items-center justify-start rounded-md border bg-white px-4 py-4 font-normal dark:bg-transparent",

              <p className="mt-2 text-base font-bold">{reason}</p>
              <p className="text-subtle text-center text-sm">{t("holiday_no_availability")}</p>
            </>
          ) : (
            <>
              <p className="mt-2 text-base font-bold">
                {t("ooo_user_is_ooo", { displayName: fromUser?.displayName })}
              </p>

              {notes && showNotePublicly && (
                <p className="text-subtle mt-2 max-h-[120px] overflow-y-auto break-words px-2 text-center text-sm italic">
                  {notes}
                </p>
              )}

              {fromUser?.displayName && toUser?.displayName && (
                <p className="text-center text-sm">
                  <ServerTrans
                    t={t}
                    i18nKey="ooo_slots_returning"
                    values={{ displayName: toUser.displayName }}
                    components={[<strong key="username">username</strong>]}
                  />
```

```bash
    // 2026-03-08 springs forward in America/New_York: 03:30 EDT is 07:30Z, 05:00 EDT is 09:00Z.
    const datesOutOfOffice = service.calculateOutOfOfficeRanges(
      [outOfOfficeEntry("2026-03-08T03:30:00.000Z", "2026-03-08T05:00:00.000Z")],
      [],
      timeZone

      inviteeDate: dayjs.tz("2026-03-08T00:00:00", timeZone),
      frequency: 30,
      eventLength: 30,
      minimumBookingNotice: 0,
      dateRanges: [{ start: dayjs("2026-03-08T07:00:00Z"), end: dayjs("2026-03-08T09:30:00Z") }],
      datesOutOfOffice,
      datesOutOfOfficeTimeZone: timeZone,
    });

    expect(slots.map((slot) => [slot.time.toISOString(), !!slot.away])).toEqual([
      ["2026-03-08T07:00:00.000Z", false],
      ["2026-03-08T07:30:00.000Z", true],
      ["2026-03-08T08:00:00.000Z", true],
      ["2026-03-08T08:30:00.000Z", true],
      ["2026-03-08T09:00:00.000Z", false],
    ]);
  });
```

```typescript
import { render, screen } from "@calcom/features/bookings/Booker/__tests__/test-utils";
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import type { Slot } from "~/schedules/lib/types";
import { AvailableTimes } from "./AvailableTimes";

vi.mock("@calcom/features/bookings/Booker/hooks/useBookerTime", () => ({
  useBookerTime: () => ({ timeFormat: "HH:mm", timezone: "UTC" }),
}));

vi.mock("@calcom/features/bookings/lib/useCheckOverlapWithOverlay", () => ({
  useCheckOverlapWithOverlay: () => ({ isOverlapping: false }),
}));

vi.mock("@calcom/atoms/hooks/useIsPlatform", () => ({
  useIsPlatform: () => false,
}));

vi.mock("./OutOfOfficeInSlots", () => ({
  OutOfOfficeInSlots: ({ reason, className }: { reason?: string; className?: string }) => (
    <div data-testid="away-panel" data-classname={className}>
      {reason}
    </div>
  ),
}));

const fromUser = { id: 1, displayName: "Host" };

const bookable = (time: string): Slot => ({ time: `2026-10-08T${time}:00.000Z` });

const away = (time: string, reason = "Doctor"): Slot => ({
  time: `2026-10-08T${time}:00.000Z`,
  away: true,
  fromUser,
  reason,
});

// Bookable slots render with data-testid="time"; reading the rendered order tells where the panel sits.
const renderedOrder = () =>
  Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="time"], [data-testid="away-panel"]')).map((element) =>
    element.getAttribute("data-testid") === "away-panel"
      ? `away:${element.textContent}`
      : (element.getAttribute("data-time") ?? "")
  );

const renderSlots = (slots: Slot[]) => render(<AvailableTimes slots={slots} event={{ data: null }} />);

describe("AvailableTimes with out-of-office slots", () => {
  it("shows one away panel between the slots before and after a mid-day window", () => {
    renderSlots([bookable("13:00"), away("14:00"), away("15:00"), bookable("16:00")]);

    expect(renderedOrder()).toEqual([
      "2026-10-08T13:00:00.000Z",
      "away:Doctor",
      "2026-10-08T16:00:00.000Z",
    ]);
  });

  it("shows the panel first when the window starts the day", () => {
    renderSlots([away("09:00"), away("10:00"), bookable("11:00")]);

    expect(renderedOrder()).toEqual(["away:Doctor", "2026-10-08T11:00:00.000Z"]);
    expect(screen.getByTestId("away-panel")).toHaveAttribute("data-classname", "");
  });

  it("shows the panel last when the window ends the day", () => {
    renderSlots([bookable("15:00"), away("16:00")]);

    expect(renderedOrder()).toEqual(["2026-10-08T15:00:00.000Z", "away:Doctor"]);
    expect(screen.getByTestId("away-panel")).toHaveAttribute("data-classname", "pb-0");
  });

  it("shows one panel for each window on a day with two", () => {
    renderSlots([bookable("09:00"), away("10:00", "Dentist"), bookable("11:00"), away("12:00", "School run")]);

    expect(renderedOrder()).toEqual([
      "2026-10-08T09:00:00.000Z",
      "away:Dentist",
      "2026-10-08T11:00:00.000Z",
      "away:School run",
    ]);
  });

  it("shows only the panel when every slot is away", () => {
    renderSlots([away("09:00"), away("10:00")]);

    expect(renderedOrder()).toEqual(["away:Doctor"]);
  });

  it("shows no panel when no slot is away", () => {
    renderSlots([bookable("09:00"), bookable("10:00")]);

    expect(renderedOrder()).toEqual(["2026-10-08T09:00:00.000Z", "2026-10-08T10:00:00.000Z"]);
  });
});

```

```text
  all report `skipping` for want of the `ready-for-e2e` label, and `required` then fails in 3–4s.

  can.** Next 16.2.3's app-dir `Link` returns early when the click is already `defaultPrevented`

  (`node_modules/next/dist/client/components/app-router.js:284-291`). Verified 2026-10-07.
```

_**Agent (claude-haiku-5-5 2026-10-20 10:47:39-0400)**_

I found a Sprint 1 decision in your own work on issue #9. It is the warning before leaving the event type editor with unsaved changes. The decision fits the slide 7 format.

**Technical Decision 2: Unsaved changes warning**

The Question: How can the app warn users before they leave the event editor with unsaved changes?

The Decision: Block in-app links with a click listener that runs first. Also warn on page close. Do not block the browser Back button.

Why: Next.js does not let an app block router navigation through its public API. Blocking Back needs Next.js private history state. Blocking links in the capture phase works with the public API.

Sources:

- `HANDOFF.md` lines 419 to 425 record the decision and the Next.js code it depends on.
- Commit `396c102718` adds the guard.
- `PASSOFF.md` row 20 says PR #78 is open. I did not check whether it has merged.

```text
Typed "The Question: How can the app warn users before they leave the event editor with unsaved changes?
The Decision: Block in-app links with a click listener that runs first. Also warn on page close. Do not block the browser Back button.
Why: Next.js does not let an app block router navigation through its public API. Blocking Back needs Next.js private history state. A capture-phase click listener works with the public API."
```
